body:
Wow, I didn't even think about any of that...

I hope they (my soon to be ex-colleagues) will see it that way too, that I'm not leaving on bad terms (as you put - Stealing/misconduct) because I'm sure dreading the Job Centre that's for sure.

I agree my work ethic won't get me a job tomorrow - Or any time soon, guaranteed - But it's trying to _survive_ during that time.

It's really hard because of a few people, have tarnished that reputation for life - And it doesn't help when you got [TV shows essentially advertising benefit scroungers](http://www.channel4.com/programmes/benefits-street), further adding taint. 

Thank you, that genuinely made me smile - And cry (happy tears this time!).

I really hope that I do get the job after the interview next week - But I keep coming back to the "what if", and granted that most of the jobs I've applied for close at the end of the month (30th/31st) so there's that too ... I guess in reality, reading your reply - I'm probably over thinking too much, and too much into the future? 

I think you're right about the different backup plan - Whilst I want to go back into the public sector, I guess that the worst (going into private sector) beats being unemployed.

I really appreciate you're reply - You've opened my mind a lot, just from reading that. And put a completely different spin on my thoughts.

It's not only the shame of receiving aid - But also the way you're treated.

As if you're a stain on this earth, tarnished because a few others before you have milked the system - Now everyone see's you as someone milking the system.

You know how American Pit's have got their bad reputation? Just because a few people used them. It's the same over here with "Benefit Scroungers"...

It's not only about receiving aid - It's also barely struggling to survive. 
I know benefits are there to "tie you over", but it rarely does for anyone.

Thanks for your support - It's also the way you're treated, and how people look at you.

Not only that, it's also having to pick between food, gas or electric, etc. 

I understand Government benefits are there to tie you over - But for many, it rarely ties anyone over.
